# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-4 (Extended v64)

## Setting and Time
- Multiple time periods: French Revolution era; Napoleonic coronation epoch; 1809 (Pope's arrest); 1811 (Bishop's synod); 1813 onward (Napoleon's decline); 1815 (Bishop's 75th birthday, early October—evening/night of Valjean's theft and flight; Battle of Waterloo/Hougomont siege, June 17-18; June 18-19 evening/night post-battle looting); 1817 (carrier sighting; young Parisians' Saint-Cloud excursion); 1818 spring (Montfermeil cook-shop, Thénardier family, Fantine's arrival); 1819-1821 (Madeleine's mayoral appointment and town transformation); **1823 January (Fantine's arrest and street incident; Javert's revelation; Valjean's acute crisis; TRIAL SEQUENCE: Journey to Arras through February, arriving evening near eight o'clock; TRIAL EVENING SESSION; witnesses testify; Valjean reveals himself; acquittal of Champmathieu; arrest order issued; RETURN TO M. SUR M. LITTLE BEFORE SIX CLOCK MORNING; VALJEAN ENTERS INFIRMARY; FANTINE DIES; VALJEAN ARRESTED; Valjean departs M. sur M. marching toward Paris carrying bundle, dressed in workman's blouse)**; **1815 June 18-19 (midnight onward: post-Waterloo looting; mysterious prowler in blouse on hollow road of Ohain; sutler's wagon hidden behind hovel at Mont-Saint-Jean to Braine-l'Alleud road angle; woman seated in wagon among coffers and packages)**; **autumn of first year / 1815 onward (trial aftermath reflected; current narrative time at Dunstead/Kelford harbor town)**; October 1823 (ship Orion enters Toulon port after heavy weather, for repairs); **November 17, 1823 (convict Jean Valjean fell from rigging into sea between Orion and frigate Algésiras, drowned, body not found, presumed entangled in Arsenal piles; newspaper account published)**; **Christmas Eve 1823 (Montfermeil tavern scene, men drinking and smoking, discussion of wine/grapes, mill operation)**; **Winter of first year (Kelford/Montfermeil, Cosette's suffering intensifies; open-air booths lit with candles in paper funnels lining from church to Thénardier hostelry; citizens preparing for midnight mass; no stars visible; toy-shop opposite Thénardier door with two-foot doll in pink crepe, gold wheat-ears, real hair, enamel eyes—marvel unaffordable to any Montfermeil mother; Cosette ventures shy glance; subsequent night: Cosette sent for water from spring, tears through darkness, enters forest at run in desperation, drops fifteen-sou piece into spring while filling bucket, struggles carrying heavy bucket back through winter forest in terror)**.
- **CURRENT NARRATIVE MOMENT**: Cosette alone in forest at night in winter carrying water bucket, age 8, struggling through darkness far from human sight; only God witnessed.
- Primary locations: M. sur M.; Montfermeil (between Livry and Chelles, southern edge of lofty plateau separating Ourcq from Marne; in 1823 small village in forest with pleasure-houses, church, spring near road to Chelles, ponds toward Gagny, water-carrier earning eight sous daily; toy-shop opposite Thénardier hostelry; Boulanger Lane); Arras; Nivelles; La Hulpe; Braine-l'Alleud; Lillois; Genappe; Hal; Tongres; Hougomont; Mont-Saint-Jean plateau; Belle-Alliance; Abbey of Villiers forest; Rossomme farm; village of Ohain; hollow road of Ohain; Chapelle-Saint-Lambert; Wavre; Dion-le-Mont; Plancenoit; forest of Paris; Papelotte; Frischemont; Boitsfort; Groenendael; Soignes forest; Waterloo battlefield; **Dunstead/Kelford (harbor town)**; Toulon port (dry dock, Arsenal quay, Arsenal point piles); Brest; Gagny; Chelles; Livry; Ravenmere; Staveford; England (Hampstead, Hull, Liverpool, Dunstead/Kelford, Suffolk, London, Welbeck Street, Lowestoft, Torton, Kelmere, Dunby, Yarlby, Ostcombe, Ravenmere); Mediterranean; Balearic Isles; Nanterre; Suresnes; Breton wheat regions; Switzerland; Pyrenees; Lille/Flanders; Brussels

## Waterloo Battle and Post-Battle Looting
[As previously recorded: sixty thousand killed; mysterious looting and prowler; hidden sutler's wagon; hollow road conditions; cuirassier officer rescue; philosophical debate on plunder; Restoration masquerade follows]

## Post-Waterloo and Restoration Era (1815-1823)
[As previously recorded: Napoleon's lingering influence; new France seeking Liberty; Congress of Vienna; Napoleon captive at Saint Helena; 1823 Spanish campaign critique; 1830 consequence germinated in 1823]

## Valjean Trial, Arrest, and Death (1823)
[As previously recorded: Trial sequence; Champmathieu acquitted; Valjean arrested and imprisoned at Toulon; assigned to convict detachment aboard ship Orion; fell from rigging November 17, 1823, presumed drowned between Orion and frigate Algésiras]

## The Orion Incident: Rescue at Toulon (October 1823)
**Ship's Condition**: Orion entered Toulon port after heavy weather; damaged from prior dry dock repairs; sprung leak near Balearic Isles; equinoctial gale damaged foretop-gallant-shrouds; later employed at Brest as school-ship

**Topman's Fall and Rescue (October 1823)**: Crew bending sails; topman fell, seized footrope; violent swinging; most sailors dared not attempt rescue; topman losing strength with horrible arm twitchings

**Convict Rescuer (Valjean)**: Man in red convict with green cap; asked permission to save topman; **broke chain riveted to ankle with one blow of hammer** (SUSPICIOUS ease); climbed with agility; reached top, cap blown away revealing perfectly white head—not young; fastened rope; descended; secured topman; held him to recover strength; left him in comrades' hands

**Fall and Death**: During descent, hesitated and staggered; fell into sea; disappeared without ripple "as though fallen into cask of oil"; body never found; four men searched until evening without result

**Metaphorical Significance**: Spider bringing life not death; moment of immense force culminating in immense feebleness affords food for thought

## Thénardier Character and Background
**Identity and History**: Composite rascal of uncertain origin—probably Fleming from Lille in Flanders; Frenchman in Paris; Belgian in Brussels; comfortably astride both frontiers; studied in Holland for inn-keeping profession; exaggerated Waterloo prowess

**Nature and Pattern**: Ebb and flow, wandering, adventure characterized his existence; tattered conscience entails fragmentary life; belonged to marauding sutlers of June 18, 1815 epoch

**Demeanor**: Peculiar rectilinear gestures recalling barracks or seminary; fine talker; appeared educated but with improper pronunciation; composed travellers' tariff card but with orthographical errors; cunning, greedy, slothful, clever

**Character Qualities**: Did not disdain servants; rarely wrathful but when enraged, terrible—bore deep furnace of hatred within; attentive and penetrating; silent or talkative by circumstance; highly intelligent; had look of sailors accustomed to screw up eyes through marine glasses; "a statesman"; possessed certain cold tranquil laugh, particularly dangerous

**Aspirations and Failure**: Single thought: enrichment; lacked theatre worthy of talent; ruining himself at Montfermeil; understood hospitality as merchandise among civilized peoples; admirable poacher with skill in shooting

**Professional Theory**: Articulated professional aphorisms: duty of inn-keeper to sell stews, repose, light, fire, dirty sheets, servant, lice, smile; stop passers-by, empty small purses, honestly lighten heavy ones; shelter travelling families respectfully; shave man, pluck woman, pick child clean; know how much shadow uses up mirror; by five hundred thousand devils, make traveller pay for everything, even for flies which his dog eats

## Female Thénardier Character
- Formidable creature; loved no one except her children; feared no one except her husband
- Mammiferous motherhood; maternity stopped short with daughters; did not extend to boys
- Jealous of husband; deemed thin, yellow man must be coveted by all; dispensed with servants
- Capable of wrath equal to husband's but his was rarer; raised cover of stew-pan; seized glass; approached cistern to use water deliberately; hideous, hyena mouth; wrath flashing in eyes; inspires terror in Cosette

## Cosette's Condition and Suffering (Winter of First Year, 1823)
**Current Status**: Age 8; serving as servant to Thénardiers at Montfermeil

**Physical Condition**: Barefooted in winter; wore rags; bare feet thrust in wooden shoes; eye black from blow of Madame Thénardier's fist; reflected with lugubrious air of old woman despite age; weak but did coarse work; thin arms; wet and tiny hands

**Labor and Treatment**: Subjected to double pressure of man and woman like creature ground in mill and pulled with pincers; each had different method—overwhelmed with blows (woman's); barefoot in winter (man's); ran upstairs and down, washed, swept, rubbed, dusted, ran, fluttered, panted, moved heavy articles; no mercy; fierce mistress and venomous master

**Household Dynamics**: Thénardier hostelry like spider's web wherein Cosette caught and trembling; ideal of oppression realized by sinister household; something like fly serving spiders

**Water Crisis**: Establishment drank little water; thirsty people never lacked there but thirst applied to jug rather than pitcher; glass of water would have appeared savage; Madame Thénardier turned faucet; thin stream trickled, half-filled glass; woman declared "there is no more water!"

**Night Errand (Winter evening, precise date unspecified)**: Sent for water from spring despite darkness and terror; descended Boulanger Lane past lighted stalls (kaleidoscope and ribbed tin lamp visible in shop windows); encountered woman who called her "the Lark"; continued into darkness beyond last lit stall; paused, scratched head, confronted choice: return to Thénardier's wrath or proceed for water; chose to flee through village and enter forest at run in desperation; ran without looking or listening; ceased only when breath failed; proceeded in desperation straight before her

**Spring Journey**: Seven or eight minutes' walk from village edge to spring; knew way from daytime visits; guided by instinct; did not turn eyes right or left for fear of seeing things in branches and brushwood; felt in dark for young oak leaning over spring; found branch, clung to it, bent down, plunged bucket in water; in state of violent excitement, strength trebled; while bent over, pocket of apron emptied—fifteen-sou piece fell into water silently; Cosette neither saw nor heard it fall; drew out bucket nearly full, set it on grass

**Return Journey (Ongoing)**: Stared at great ruddy star near horizon traversing dense mist—unfamiliar, terrified her; planet resembled luminous wound; seized by black enormity of nature; something more terrible than terror; shivered with strangeness chilling to very bottom of heart; eye grew wild; thought she should not be able to refrain from returning at same hour on morrow; began counting aloud one through ten to escape singular state; restored true perception; hands wet from drawing water felt cold; rose; terror natural and unconquerable returned; one thought only—flee at full speed through forest, across fields to houses, windows, lighted candles; yet dared not flee without bucket of water due to Thénardier's fright-inducing power; seized handle with both hands; could hardly lift pail; advanced dozen paces but bucket full and heavy; forced to set on ground, take breath, resume march; walked bent forward with drooping head like old woman; weight of bucket strained and stiffened thin arms; iron handle completed benumbing and freezing of wet and tiny hands; forced to halt from time to time; cold water splashing from pail fell on bare legs; proceeded alone in depths of forest at night in winter far from all human sight; no one but God saw that sad thing at the moment

**Emotional/Psychological State**: Melancholy; consciousness of oppression; terror of Thénardier more powerful than forest fear; desperation; involuntary compulsion to return; state of bewilderment and confusion

## Montfermeil Village Description (1823)
- Located between Livry and Chelles on southern edge of plateau separating Ourcq from Marne
- Small village in forest with pleasure-houses of last century with twisted iron balconies, long windows with tiny panes
- Water rare due to plateau elevation: end toward Gagny drew from forest ponds; other end found water only at spring halfway down slope near road to Chelles, quarter hour walk from village; large houses paid water-carrier (earning eight sous daily) half farthing per bucketful; shuttered at five o'clock winter, seven o'clock summer
- **Toy-shop**: Established precisely opposite Thénardier door, glittering with tinsel, glass, magnificent tin objects; displayed immense doll nearly two feet high dressed in pink crepe robe with gold wheat-ears on head, real hair and enamel eyes on background of white napkins; marvel displayed to wonderment of all passers-by under ten years of age without mother sufficiently rich or extravagant to purchase; Éponine and Azelma passed hours contemplating it; Cosette ventured shy glance

## Dunstead/Kelford Community: Ongoing Daily Life
- **Pewyn**: counted coins twice, penny short; gave Nylia Corrford solemn promise to rebuild fallen wall at Quenford (COMMITMENT)
- **Yewyn Corrford** (also called Yewyn Haskick): appeared tired; bought ribbon, regretted it; asked Lura if it will rain; agreed with Kassa about salt price scandal; **married Tatho Brackick at Ravenmere before spring was out** (FACT, winter 1823-1824); couple lived in Ravenmere from then on
- **Ulrald Corrford**: complained of aching back; gave Lura Haskick solemn promise to pay old debt owed to Stenson family (COMMITMENT); counted coins twice, penny short
- **Nylia Corrford**: complained of aching back; gave Pewyn solemn promise to rebuild fallen wall at Quenford (COMMITMENT); read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half the saints; laughed at story nobody else found funny
- **Yera Haskick**: gave Yewyn Corrford solemn promise to carry sealed letter to Dungate (COMMITMENT); late one night confided to Kassa Brackick that Stenenridge mill ledger was rewritten after the flood (CLAIM)
- **Lura Haskick**: recipient of Ulrald's debt-payment promise; mended torn sleeve by window, said little; shrugged when asked about rain
- **Kassa Brackick**: told Yewyn "price of salt is scandal"; received Yera's confidence about mill ledger; fell asleep in chair before fire caught
- **Elra Corrford**: spent evening sorting old letters by candlelight; watched clouds, predicted rain wrongly; walked long way round to avoid muddy square; told Marald he looked tired
- **Marald Corrford**: asked about rain; confirmed looking tired
- **Tatho Brackick**: rode out of Kelford; by next market day living in Ravenmere; **married Yewyn Corrford at Ravenmere before spring was out** (FACT); couple lived in Ravenmere from then on
- **Rozek Stenenridge**: burned letter after reading; found work in Staveford, moved there, did not return; **CLAIM**: Luena followed him to Staveford within the month
- **Volia/Volia Brackick**: talked of weather, harvest, lame horse; **laughed at story nobody else found funny**; mended torn sleeve by window and said little
- **Kadrek/Kadrek Brackick**: argued with carter over price of sack of oats
- **Fenelle**: read almanac aloud, mispronouncing half the saints

**Environmental backdrop**: Ruts and puddles after thaw; crooked sun chalked on forge wall; smoke lay flat over fields; baker's boy late, line at oven grew long; frost silvered hedges; bell for vespers rang thinly; children chased hoop; cart with turnips creaked past well; dog barked then went quiet; wind off water smelled of salt and tar; bees hummed in lavender behind parsonage; gulls quarreled over fish heads by steps; rain threatened but held off; open-air booths illuminated with candles in paper funnels lining from church to hostelry; citizens preparing for midnight mass; no stars visible; light went early as it did that time of year; road all ruts and puddles after thaw

## Montfermeil Tavern Scene (Christmas Eve 1823)
- Number of men (carters, peddlers) seated drinking and smoking around four or five candles in public room
- Room resembled all drinking-shops: tables, pewter jugs, bottles, drinkers, smokers; little light, great noise
- Fashionable bourgeois objects: kaleidoscope and ribbed tin lamp
- Female Thénardier attending to supper roasting before clear fire; husband drinking with customers, talking politics
- Discussion topics: vines near Nanterre and Suresnes flourishing; grapes, juice, wine quality; Breton wheat grinding problems (contains tares, fennel, vetches, hempseed, fox-tail, pebbles); miller complaints about grain quality
- Éponine and Azelma's laughter audible from adjoining room; very young boy (born preceding winter, age three or less) crying persistently in dark; mother did not love him, called him "the result of the cold"; child continued shrieking when clamor became annoying

## Main Characters Status
- **Jean Valjean**: Dead (drowned November 17, 1823, at Toulon)
- **Fantine**: Dead (buried in pauper's grave, January 1823)
- **Cosette**: Suffering under Thénardier household at Montfermeil, age 8; currently alone in forest at night carrying water bucket in terror
- **Napoleon Bonaparte**: Defeated, imprisoned at Saint Helena

## Themes
- Destiny/chance; divine intervention; human resilience against oppression
- Waterloo as historical hinge; war's moral paradox; marauding and plunder
- Mundane life indifferent to empires; daily tasks continue beneath grand narratives
- Mystery/obscurity: Boulatruelle's search; Valjean's suspicious chain-breaking ease; mill ledger rewritten; sealed letter; letters burned
- Hidden transgressions and buried truths; lost coin in spring
- Human courage in extremis: Valjean risking life for stranger; topman clinging to rope; child enduring suffering and proceeding alone through winter forest
- Immense force culminating in immense feebleness affords food for thought
- Poverty and exploitation: Cosette's servitude; water scarcity; Thénardiers' neglect of own children; exploitation as professional system
- Parasitic exploitation; commerce of suffering; hospitality as merchandise
- Terror of the night; natural horror; psychological compulsion; one child witnessed only by God
